podcast.title: Roadie Yellow Feather Identifier
podcast.body: For The Raconteurs, roadies wore a distinctive yellow feather stuck in the brim of their fedoras, serving as a visual identifier for the crew working for the band. "If a roadie has a yellow feather stuck in the room of his head, he's working for the Rock on Tours."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Multiple Music Projects
xref.body: Jack White is involved in several music projects, all associated with his independent label, Third Man Records. These include The White Stripes, The Raconteurs, and The Dead Weather. "ranging from Jack White and the white stripes and the rack on tours and the dead weather, which are all Jack's projects, of course, to Conan O'Brien and Johnny Cash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Roadie Uniform Aesthetic
xref.body: Jack White is known for incorporating distinct roadie uniforms into his shows for both The White Stripes and The Raconteurs. Roadies are typically dressed in black suits, white shirts, black ties, and black fedoras, reflecting White's belief that the crew's attire is part of the visual spectacle. "Jack believes that the roadie uniform can be part of the overall visual spectacle of a gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
